t:
(a) In General.—The boundary of the Monument is revised to include an area totaling approximately 70 acres, as generally depicted on the Map.
 
    (b) Availability of Map.—The Map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Director of the National Park Service.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "available for public inspection" brings the public into the process. It only makes a map viewable after Congress itself has revised the boundary; no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to comment on or challenge a federal decision. Transparency about a completed decision is not participation.
fable.s: The Map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Director of the National Park Service.

qwen_block.w: The section requires that a map defining the monument's boundary be available for 'public inspection.' This grants the general public (an outside party) access to information relevant to a federal decision (the boundary revision), which constitutes a form of participation under the definition. While it is not a hearing or comment period, making official records available for public inspection is a mechanism for public engagement with government actions.
qwen_block.s: The Map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Director of the National Park Service.

opus.w: The section revises a monument boundary directly and requires the map to be kept on file for public viewing. Public inspection of a map is one-way disclosure: it gives outsiders no role in the decision, such as a comment period, hearing, consultation or right to object. The word "public" makes participation tempting, but no outside party takes part in any federal decision.
opus.s: The Map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Director of the National Park Service.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "available for public inspection" brings in the public. It doesn't. Making a map available only lets people look at a decision that has already been made. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted or given a way to comment, object or sue before the decision. Congress revises the boundary directly in the text itself.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely requires that a map be available for public inspection. It does not require the government to consult with the public, hold a hearing, or seek comments before making the decision to revise the monument boundary. Access to information is not the same as participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Map shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Director of the National Park Service.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that making a map "available for public inspection" constitutes public participation because it allows the public to access information. However, the definition specifies that participation involves consulting or coordinating with outsiders *before* making a decision, or involving them in advisory bodies, hearings, etc. Merely providing access to a document after a decision has been made (or as part of administrative transparency) does not constitute the interactive decision-making process defined as participation. There is no requirement for public comment, hearing, or consultation regarding the boundary revision itself in this text.
